h: A prep-school dropout wanders New York for a weekend, griping and wisecracking his way around a grief he never names.

like.r: Another disaffected young narrator in a phony-feeling 1950s world, with the same confiding voice and a darker private collapse.
The same era's restless, misunderstood teenager, shown on screen rather than in his own sardonic words.
The older American runaway-narrator novel, with a sharper eye on society and a river instead of a city.

h: A seductive, wickedly funny prose stylist narrates his own crime, and the book makes you notice how charm can bury a victim.

like.r: Another self-justifying narrator circling his own guilt, with feverish psychology in place of Nabokov's glittering wordplay.
A charming, amoral voice you follow against your better judgment, in a cooler and much plainer prose style.
Nabokov's own screenplay adapted by Kubrick, which pushes the dark comedy forward and keeps the worst of it offstage.

h: A tomboy narrates one Alabama summer and the trial her lawyer father takes on; gentle on the surface, firm about injustice.

like.r: A faithful, warmly acted adaptation that makes the courtroom scenes the heart of the story.
Another Southern story of racial cruelty told in a plain, intimate voice, though far more raw about what Black women endured.
A Mississippi trial that tests a small town's conscience, paced like a thriller rather than a memory piece.

t: Go Tell It on the Mountain
h: One Harlem Saturday and a boy's 14th birthday open onto his family's buried past, told in prose that sounds like a sermon.

like.r: Another landmark of Black American identity in the same era, angrier and more surreal where Baldwin is devout and intimate.
Shares the incantatory prose and the way family history presses on the present, with a ghost story at its center.
A lush, tender screen adaptation of another Baldwin novel set in the same Harlem world of love under pressure.

h: An American in Paris runs from his own desire into a doomed affair; a short, aching novel about shame and what it costs.

like.r: Another summer-bright, wounding same-sex romance remembered in a hungry first-person voice, but gentler about its ending.
Closeted love crushed by the world around it, shown with the same quiet devastation.
A queer coming-of-age tale, cooler and more satirical, set in 1980s London high society.

h: A nameless Black narrator moves from the South to Harlem and finds every institution wants him to be somebody else.

like.r: A harder, more naturalistic portrait of a Black man crushed by American society, with none of Ellison's surreal comedy.
The ancestor of the bitter, self-dissecting underground narrator, here in a short furious confession.
A similarly absurd, circular institutional nightmare, played for black comedy in wartime.

h: A gifted young woman wins a summer in New York and then slides into depression; sharp, darkly funny and hard to shake.

like.r: The male counterpart of this alienated, confiding voice, funnier and less clinical about its breakdown.
A young woman in a 1960s psychiatric hospital, drawn from a memoir and in tune with Plath's mix of wit and dread.
A short earlier classic of a woman's mind unraveling under the control of others, more gothic and claustrophobic.

t: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
h: A brawling con fakes madness to dodge prison work and picks a fight with a ward run by a terrifyingly polite nurse.

like.t: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
like.r: A beloved, tightly acted film that shifts the point of view away from the narrator but keeps the ward's menace.
Another comic fight against an inhuman institution, this time in wartime, with more circular absurdity.
The darker, more political version of a lone man crushed by a system that demands conformity.

h: A bombardier just wants to survive, but every rule of his army is a loop that traps him; jokes circle back as horror.

like.r: Another war novel that treats the absurd as the only honest register, shorter and more tender.
The same deadpan insistence that the people running the war machine are lunatics, on a Cold War stage.
An earlier comic war novel in which a holy fool exposes military bureaucracy by following orders too well.

h: A soldier comes unstuck in time after the firebombing of Dresden; a short, deadpan book that laughs so it won't scream.

like.r: The other great American war satire, longer and more frenetic, with the same refusal to be heroic.

like.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
like.r: Shares the shrugging absurd humor and a cosmic view of human folly, in a lighter comic-SF key.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: A tender story that also scrambles time to show how memory shapes a life, though far more romantic.

h: A narrator tracing the inventor of the atom bomb stumbles on a made-up religion and a substance that could end the world.

like.r: The author's other short, mordant masterstroke, with war and time travel in place of invented religion.
Scientists and politicians stumbling toward the end of the world with unshakable confidence, as black comedy.
An earlier satire about technology and engineered belief, a bit more systematic and a lot less jokey.

h: Seven generations of the Buendía family rise and fade in a jungle town where miracles and civil wars feel equally ordinary.

like.t: Love in the Time of Cholera
like.r: The same author's more focused tale of a single, patient passion over half a century.
Another sprawling national history told through magical happenings and a family, with a more comic, restless voice.
A multi-generational Latin American family epic with magic in the margins, more political and more direct.

t: Love in the Time of Cholera
h: A man waits more than fifty years for the woman who refused him; a lush, wry look at obsession that passes for devotion.

like.r: The author's wider, stranger epic of a family and a town, with less romance and more myth.
Another life of unspoken love and lost years, narrated by a man in denial, in a much more restrained key.
A hushed, aching film about love that cannot be acted on, shorter and more repressed.

h: A surgeon and his lovers in Soviet-crushed Prague, interrupted by the narrator's essays on weight, kitsch and chance.

like.r: A fellow Prague writer on helpless individuals before an absurd system, darker and without the erotic comedy.
Another short, essayistic novel that reasons about memory and regret with dry intelligence.
A sensual adaptation that captures the love triangle and the Prague Spring, though the philosophical asides fade.

h: A formerly enslaved woman in Ohio is haunted by the child she lost, and by a past that insists on being told.

like.r: Another unsparing look at slavery's physical and psychic horror, plainer in style but with a speculative twist.
Black women's survival of brutality told with a more direct voice and an ending that leans toward grace.
A harrowing, unflinching true account of enslavement that shares the novel's refusal to look away.

h: A comfortable, aimless Black man in Michigan chases a family legend of gold and flight and finds his ancestry.

like.r: The author's darker, more devastating novel about family history, more ghostly and more intense.
Another family saga that treats the marvelous and the mythic as part of everyday history.
A parallel quest for Black American selfhood, angrier and more satirical in its sweep.

h: In 1940s Ohio a Black girl prays for blue eyes in a world that says she is ugly; a short, devastating debut.

like.r: The author's masterwork on trauma, with a sprawling ghost story where this one stays closer to the ground.

like.t: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
like.r: A Black girl's childhood in the Jim Crow South, told as memoir with more resilience and warmth.
A similar story of abused girls and women finding their voices, with a more redemptive course.

h: A father and son walk a burnt, ashen America toward the coast with a gun and almost nothing else; relentlessly grim, quietly loving.

like.r: A grey and faithful adaptation that keeps the book's despair and the bond between father and son.
A gentler post-collapse novel about what we save, with art and hope where McCarthy leaves only love.
The author's brutal western, with the same biblical severity but far more violence and no tenderness.

h: A teenage runaway joins a scalp-hunting gang in the 1850s borderlands; biblical prose wrapped around staggering cruelty.

like.r: The older American epic of obsession and cosmic menace, with the same grand, scriptural cadence on the water instead of the desert.
Another definitive western from the same year, far warmer, funnier and more humane about frontier life.
A punishing frontier survival tale with a similar mix of beauty and brutality, much simpler in its story.

h: A hunter finds a drug deal's wreckage and two million dollars, and a relentless killer starts closing in across West Texas.

like.r: A near-literal adaptation with unbearable tension and a Javier Bardem villain who sets the standard.
The author's other lean, hopeless later novel, more intimate and with a father's love at its center.
Another bloody crime story about greed and chance, but wryly funny and set in snowy Minnesota.

h: Two Texas teenagers ride to Mexico in 1949 chasing a vanished way of life; tender, elegiac and then suddenly brutal.

like.r: A longer, warmer western of friends on a long ride, with the same mourning for a vanishing West.
The author's far more violent and apocalyptic vision of the same borderlands.
A young person's western journey with dry humor and formal speech, lighter and quicker.

h: A woman forced into reproductive servitude in a theocratic America narrates her thin hold on herself in clipped, cold detail.

like.r: The classic state-control dystopia that Atwood updates for gender and bodies, more political and less personal.
A modern feminist speculation that flips the gender balance of violence, brisker and more lurid.
Another near-future nightmare about fertility and authoritarianism, as a thriller of chases and long takes.

h: A young servant convicted of a double murder tells her story to a doctor, and you cannot decide whether to believe her.

like.r: A Victorian novel of class, secrets and double-crossing women, more plot-driven and with bigger reversals.
Atwood's other layered novel of buried truths and unreliable testimony, with a nested pulp story.
A shorter, more fevered novel about a woman judged mad and a self told through other people's versions.

h: An old woman recalls her dead sister's life and the pulp science fiction tale inside it; nested stories with a sharp edge.

like.r: Another layered novel in which a woman's own telling hides guilt and a sister's fate.
A first-person tale shadowed by a dead woman and a guarded secret, more gothic and less formal.
Another Atwood puzzle about a woman whose history may not be what she says, in Victorian Canada.

h: An English butler drives west on a short holiday and, between lapses of dignity, lets slip what his loyalty cost him.

like.r: A restrained, beautifully acted film in which what goes unsaid is the whole story.
Another English country-house tale about a self-serving memory and the harm of a single misreading.
The author's other novel of a narrator who quietly accepts a fate, in a strange boarding-school world.

h: Three friends from an English boarding school slowly realize what they are for; gentle, restrained and hard to forget.

like.r: A quiet, faithful adaptation with a dim light that mirrors the book's resignation.
Another near-future novel of bodies controlled by the state, with more anger and less acquiescence.
Ishiguro's later novel with a different kind of artificial being and the same quiet, wounded tone.

h: A man born at the instant of India's independence finds his fate tied to the nation, in a torrent of jokes, smells and miracles.

like.r: The magical-realist national epic that Rushdie draws on, with a gentler, more mythic tone.
Another history-soaked novel narrated by an eccentric, unreliable outsider who ties himself to a nation's crimes.
Another Indian family story with lush, playful language, narrower in scope and more tragic.

h: Two Indian actors fall from a hijacked plane over England and are transformed; a wild, dense novel about migration and belief.

like.r: An older satire that sends a naive traveler across the world to mock faith and certainty, much shorter and drier.
Rushdie's more accessible and still dazzling national epic, with less theology.
A funnier, more accessible portrait of immigrant families in London, with the same energy of voice.

h: A Jewish New Yorker confesses to his analyst in one long, filthy, hilarious rant about his mother, his guilt and his desires.

like.r: Another neurotic Jewish intellectual in comic crisis, more learned and more tender.
Another novel built on one grotesque, hilarious complainer, here a slothful scholar in New Orleans.
The same self-lacerating Jewish New York comedy of therapy and women, in a warmer, lighter register.

h: A golden high-school athlete builds the perfect American life, then his daughter bombs the local post office.

like.r: A Midwestern family unraveling in the shadow of American illusions, funnier and more contemporary.
Another suburban dream curdling around a couple, sharper and colder in its judgment.
Another portrait of suburban surface and private upheaval, played as dark comedy.

h: A professor of Hitler studies frets about death while a toxic cloud drifts toward his college town; dry, eerie and very funny.

like.r: The author's vast American panorama, with the same fascination for waste and fear but on a far larger scale.
A shorter, jokier take on how modern science and consumer life hum above the abyss.
Another absurdist, deadpan satire of bureaucratic modern life, more surreal and more visual.

h: A baseball and a waste executive's memory stitch together half a century of Cold War America in a sprawling, dazzling book.

like.r: Another huge, paranoid American epic of systems and secret history, more difficult and more unruly.
The author's far shorter, funnier, more focused novel on death and consumer anxiety.
Another look at postwar America's promise and decay, centered on one family instead of a whole era.

h: A novelist raised by a famous feminist mother meets absurd accidents and violence; comic, tender and deeply worried about kids.

like.r: The author's other great New England novel, with a stranger hero and a greater sense of fate.
A quieter, more moral Irving tale of an orphan, a doctor and a difficult choice.
Another eccentric, fond portrait of a gifted, damaged family, tidier and more stylized.

h: A tiny boy with a wrecked voice believes he is God's instrument, and his best friend narrates a life shaped by that faith.

like.r: Irving's earlier outsized comedy of accidents and family, less spiritual and more violent.
A boy's voice that carries the novel, here with a New England wit and a missing mother.
Another quiet novel about faith and friendship in small-town America, more meditative and less comic.

h: An orphan raised by an abortion-providing doctor must decide what to do with the rules he is given; humane and old-fashioned.

like.r: The author's other moving novel on fate, friendship and faith in New England.
A gently shaped adaptation written by Irving himself, trimming the sprawl and keeping the heart.
The classic orphan-and-institution tale that Irving openly echoes, broader in its villains and warmer in its coincidences.

h: A scholarship outsider joins an elite classics clique at a Vermont college, and the murder is told in the first pages.

like.r: An outsider enthralled by a glamorous, doomed circle at university, nostalgic where Tartt is menacing.
A narrator seduced by a glittering world he can't join and watches fall apart, much shorter.
A prep school clique under a charismatic teacher's spell, far warmer and more inspiring about where it leads.

h: A Tokyo student in the late 1960s is pulled between two women while grief for a friend's suicide settles over everything.

like.r: Another wry, melancholy young narrator working through a death, in an earlier American key.
The author's stranger, more fantastical coming-of-age, with cats and metaphysics instead of realism.
A quiet, drifting Tokyo story of loneliness and connection with the same wistful mood.

h: A jobless man's cat and then his wife disappear, and he descends a dry well into a strange underworld of history and dreams.

like.r: A shorter, more playful Murakami with two interleaved quests and talking cats.
Another bewildering book where an ordinary man is caught in an inexplicable system, older, shorter and drier.
A dream-logic mystery that likewise refuses neat answers and rewards the mood more than the solution.

h: A runaway teenager and an old man who talks to cats move toward each other through libraries, oracles and raining fish.

like.r: Murakami's darker, longer descent into the subconscious through a drifting, ordinary man.
A simpler, more fable-like journey of a youth following signs, much lighter on the strangeness.
A young person's passage through an uncanny parallel world, with the same dreamlike logic and wonder.

h: An aging Midwestern couple tries to gather their three disappointing adult children for one last Christmas; sharp and funny.

like.r: A comparable big social comedy of family and generations, bigger on race and London.
A heavier portrait of a family and country in disrepair, with more anger and less comic relief.
Another damaged family reunion, lighter and more stylized.

h: Two war buddies and their families tumble through multicultural London over decades of fanaticism, friendship and mishaps.

like.r: The more magical, more history-laden ancestor of Smith's busy, immigrant-minded comedy.
Another sprawling, funny, clear-eyed family novel, set in the American Midwest.
An earlier, more intimate London story of immigrant ambition and desire, wry about race and class.

h: Two feuding professors and their families collide at a Boston college; a comedy of manners about art, race and betrayal.

like.r: The clear model for the novel, in which two very different families are tied together by class and chance.
The author's first, wilder, more chaotic London ensemble.
Another stylish comedy of manners about privilege, art and desire among a politically connected family in 1980s London.

h: A narrator born intersex traces the family secret from a Greek village through Detroit; warm, sprawling and funny.

like.r: The author's much smaller, eerier suburban novel, with a collective narrator and a very different mood.
Another voice-heavy history of a nation and a family, with magical ingredients and a body that stands in for it.
Another big Midwestern family novel with sharp humor, less comfortable about identity.

h: The boys across the street spend years piecing together why five sisters ended their lives; dreamy, wistful and unsettling.

like.r: A hazy, pastel adaptation that is as obsessed with mood as the book.
The inside view of a young woman's depression, rawer and far less dreamy.
Another sun-drenched mystery of vanished girls that is never solved, and is all about longing.

h: A 13-year-old's false accusation wrecks a love affair on a hot English afternoon, and the consequences ripple through the war.

like.r: A gorgeous, tense film with a famous long take at Dunkirk and a faithful sense of the book's structure.
Another English novel of an unreliable self-telling and a love lost to propriety, calmer and more restrained.
A wartime love story with the same lush prose, more fragmented and more exotic.

h: Two old friends, a composer and an editor, make a vow after a funeral and let their self-regard drag them to ruin.

like.r: The author's later, more emotionally ambitious novel on guilt, with real heart as well as irony.
A similarly cool tale of amorality, with a creepier lead and more suspense.
A London drama in which chance and self-interest destroy moral certainty, with the same icy tone.

t: The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay
h: Two Jewish cousins invent a comic-book superhero in 1939 New York while their family fights to escape Europe; joyful and sad.

like.r: Another playful Jewish-American novel of history and inheritance, more experimental.
A bighearted American coming-of-age novel with the same bounding prose, set in Depression Chicago.
A love letter to the art that shapes a life, as nostalgic and sentimental about a medium.

h: Five parts follow critics, a journalist and a mystic across Europe and a Mexican border city where women keep dying; vast, bleak, hypnotic.

like.r: The author's earlier, livelier novel of poets in motion, equally sprawling but far more playful.
A desert borderland haunted by mass violence, in denser, more mythic prose.
Another enormous, many-threaded novel that rewards patience, closer to comedy and addiction.

h: A diarist, then dozens of witnesses, trace two vanished poets through Mexico City, Europe and Africa across twenty years.

like.r: Bolaño's darker, bigger, final novel, with the same piecemeal mystery and far less youthful fun.
The restless road novel of artists and friends in motion that Bolaño honors and complicates.

like.t: The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao
like.r: A voice-forward, geeky, literary novel of exile and generations, more comic and more focused.

h: A girl in Nigeria watches her devout, controlling father rule their home with violence, until a stay with her aunt opens a window.

like.r: The foundational Nigerian novel of a patriarch undone by pride, wider in history and older in time.
Another postcolonial family tragedy seen through young eyes, more ornate and playful.
Another story of a girl finding herself after domestic violence, told in letters and a vibrant voice.

h: Three lives in Nigeria are pulled apart by the Biafran war, moving from sunlit parties to starvation.

like.r: The older, shorter Nigerian classic that lays the colonial groundwork for the country's later crises.
Another novel in which ordinary women endure a country's wars, equally emotional and more melodramatic.
A humane African conflict story told from inside a city under siege.

h: An Afghan boy betrays his closest friend and spends decades trying to make amends; blunt, emotional and hard to put down.

like.r: Hosseini's follow-up swaps the guilt-ridden man for two women and their shared fight to survive.
Another popular, tearful story of a child's loyalty and loss during a terrible war.
A faithful adaptation with Afghan-language dialogue that captures the kites and the heartbreak.

h: Two Afghan women, married to the same brutal man, form a bond across thirty years of war and Taliban rule.

like.r: The more male-centered Hosseini debut about friendship, betrayal and exile.
Another woman-centered story of private lives shattered by a national war, richer in nuance.
Women supporting each other against domestic cruelty, in a different place and a more hopeful form.

h: A boy is shipwrecked on a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger; a story about faith and survival that asks what you choose to believe.

like.r: A visually stunning adaptation that makes the ocean and the tiger a spectacle.

like.t: The Old Man and the Sea
like.r: A short, spare tale of one man, one animal and the sea, quieter and tougher.
The original castaway survival story, more practical and earthbound than Martel's fable.

h: Death narrates a foster girl's life in Nazi Germany, where she steals books and hides a Jewish man in the basement.

like.t: The Diary of a Young Girl
like.r: The real-life counterpart of a girl's wartime hiding, plain and immediate rather than lyrical.

like.t: The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas
like.r: Another Holocaust story through a child's naive eyes, blunter and more manipulative.
A comparable weepy, accessible novel about a child's moral failure and loyalty, in Afghanistan.

h: Two retired Texas Rangers drive a herd to Montana; a long, funny, heartbreaking ride that is mostly about friendship.

like.r: The bleak mirror of the frontier, far more violent and mythic, with none of McMurtry's warmth.
An elegiac, adult western about aging gunmen and the cost of legends.
A shorter, drier western adventure with a sharp narrator and a mismatched trio.

h: An English pilot is shipwrecked in feudal Japan and caught in a samurai power struggle; vast, immersive, hard to stop.

like.r: Another door-stopper of intrigue and ambition across years, set in medieval England.
A Westerner immersed in Japanese warrior culture, in a faster, more romantic film.
Another popular window on Japanese culture seen through an outsider's version, with a feminine rather than martial focus.

h: Generations of builders, bishops and bandits fight over a cathedral in twelfth-century England; a thick, binge-able saga.

like.r: Another sprawling, plot-rich historical epic of ambition and politics, set in feudal Japan.
Another court-and-power novel, in Tudor England, slower and more literary.
A medieval epic of faith and ambition on a grand scale, with swordplay in place of masonry.

h: A fisherman's daughter is sold into a Kyoto geisha house and rises through rivalry and longing in a vanishing world.

like.r: A lush, sumptuous adaptation that trades interiority for costumes and visual beauty.

like.t: Snow Flower and the Secret Fan
like.r: Another novel of women's friendship and constraint in an older Asian world.
A male-driven and violent view of the same country's history, more political and more martial.

h: A zealous Baptist preacher drags his wife and four daughters to the Congo in 1959, and each woman tells what it did to them.

like.r: The African side of colonial disruption, shorter, harder and told from within the culture.
The darker, shorter classic of the Congo and imperial folly, with none of Kingsolver's humane humor.
Another novel in which several women in one family take turns telling their stories.

h: A poor Black Georgia woman writes letters to God and then to her sister, and slowly finds her own voice and worth.

like.r: A darker, more lyrical novel of Black women's suffering and survival, with a ghost story at its center.
A warm, big-hearted adaptation anchored by great performances, gentler about the book's cruelty.

like.t: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
like.r: A real-life account of a Black girl's survival in the segregated South, told with similar frankness.

h: A proud Igbo wrestler's world is dismantled by missionaries and colonial officials; spare, short and quietly devastating.

like.r: The colonial view of Africa that Achebe wrote against, more atmospheric and less humane to Africans.
A later Nigerian novel that picks up the country's history in the civil war, richer in characters.
A colonial-era encounter told from the Western family's side, longer and more voice-driven.

h: A dying Iowa minister writes a long letter to his young son about faith, family and the beauty of ordinary days.

like.r: Robinson's first novel, with the same hushed, glowing prose, about two sisters and their eccentric aunt.
Another novel of faith and friendship in an American small town, funnier and more plot-heavy.
A film in the same register of reverence and memory, even more abstract.

h: Two orphaned sisters live with an unconventional aunt in a flood-prone lakeside town; a short book that glows with strange beauty.

like.r: Robinson's later, warmer novel in the same luminous voice, but about faith and fatherhood.
Another dreamlike tale of odd girls in a small American town, more eerie.
Another outsider story in a cold northern place, funnier and more plot-driven.

h: A former high-school basketball star walks out on his pregnant wife and drifts through small-town Pennsylvania; sensual and unsparing.

like.r: A harder, more claustrophobic portrait of a stifled American marriage in the same era.
The wilder, more romantic version of the man who leaves, written with a jazz-like looseness.
Another aimless young American drifting away from the life laid out for him, with a lot more comedy and a lot less guilt.

h: A young couple who think they are too special for suburbia come undone in front of their neighbors; a painfully accurate marriage autopsy.

like.r: Another novel of a restless man and a stifled marriage, with more sensuous prose and less sympathy.
A harrowing adaptation, with DiCaprio and Winslet fighting it out in beautiful, stifling rooms.
A vicious play of one night of marital warfare, even louder and drunker.

h: A pompous, slothful medievalist in New Orleans stumbles through jobs, schemes and hot dog carts; outrageously funny.

like.r: Another sprawling farce of grotesque characters and circular logic, set in wartime.
Another bitterly funny novel built on a single monstrous, self-obsessed voice.
A slacker's picaresque through the strange characters of a city, similarly funny and shaggy.

h: Two tailors, a widow and a student share a flat in 1970s Bombay during the Emergency; long, humane and heartbreaking.

like.r: Another Indian family novel of injustice, more lyrical and more compact.
Another story of ordinary people crushed by political events, written in a plainer, more melodramatic voice.
A brighter, faster look at Indian poverty and street survival, with some of the same warmth.

h: Fraternal twins in Kerala remember the summer that a forbidden love and a drowning wrecked their family; dazzling, mournful language.

like.r: The louder, funnier Indian novel of history and fate, with similar play on language.
A wider, plainer novel of Indian social injustice.
Another family history rendered as myth, with time folding over itself.

h: A burned pilot, a nurse, a thief and a sapper wait out the war in a ruined Italian villa as his story of love in the desert surfaces.

like.r: A sweeping, romantic adaptation that makes the desert love story its center.
Another wartime novel of love and its damage, more plotted and less poetic.
Another slow, lyrical wartime odyssey of a wounded man trying to reach a woman.

h: A wounded Confederate deserter walks home through the broken South to a woman he barely knows, while she learns to farm alone.

like.r: The romantic Civil War epic that Frazier quietly rebukes, with an unsentimental look at the home front.
Another wartime love story told in beautiful, fragmented prose.
A well-acted adaptation that gives the journey and the war its visual sweep.

h: A retired historian in a wheelchair reconstructs his grandparents' marriage in the mining West, and measures it against his own.

like.r: Another major novel of the American West, bigger and warmer, with cowboys rather than letters.
Another quiet, retrospective novel of a family, in a gentler and more spiritual key.
An earlier, shorter frontier novel with similar reverence for the land and the people who settle it.

h: A Japanese-American fisherman stands trial for murder on a foggy Pacific island, where old wartime wounds lie under the snow.

like.r: A more optimistic, accessible courtroom drama about prejudice in a small community.
Another novel about one false or half-seen act poisoning a community and a love story.
A lovely, gray-blue adaptation that leans into the book's weather and mood.

h: A bruised, shy newspaperman moves with his daughter to a windswept Newfoundland fishing town and slowly thaws.

like.r: Another cold-weather novel of damaged people finding their way, quieter and stranger.
Another novel of weather and wounded people finding a way back, in a different century.
Another bleakly funny portrait of a snowbound community, only crueler.

h: The mad first wife in Jane Eyre's attic gets her own story, a feverish Caribbean childhood and a marriage that ruins her.

like.r: The classic gothic romance that Rhys answers, with the madwoman's view turned inside out.
Another novel that gives voice to a woman the official story erased, in a richly haunted register.
Another gothic marriage shadowed by a dead or discarded first wife, more suspenseful and less political.

h: V-2 rockets fall on London and an American lieutenant's mind seems linked to them; a huge, paranoid, filthy-funny puzzle.

like.r: Another monumental, footnoted American novel of systems and obsession, funnier and more emotionally direct.
The far more readable war satire of absurd bureaucracy and paranoia.
A big Cold War novel of hidden systems, written in a cooler, less gonzo style.

h: A California housewife named executor of an ex-lover's estate follows clues toward a secret postal underground, or her own madness.

like.r: Pynchon's mammoth masterpiece, with the same paranoia magnified into a thousand pages.
A paranoid investigator in a hidden-system world, with a more serious tone and less comedy.
Another mystery of signs and conspiracies that delights in ambiguity, set in a medieval abbey.

h: A tennis academy, a halfway house and a lethal film cartridge collide in a huge, footnoted novel about addiction and entertainment.

like.r: The darker, harder ancestor of the encyclopedic American novel, with paranoid plots in place of addiction.
A much shorter, drier satire of media and death that is a good way into this style.
A more accessible big novel of the era's anxieties, by Wallace's friend and rival.

t: The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao
h: A sci-fi-obsessed Dominican-American nerd and his family are chased by a curse and a dictator's long shadow, in a thunderous voice.

like.r: Another immigrant-family comedy with big energy and big ideas, in London.
Another Latin American novel that mixes street talk, literature and exile.
The model for a history told by a rowdy voice, with magical ingredients.

h: Six nested stories, from a Pacific diary to a far-future oral tale, hand off to one another like Russian dolls.

like.t: If on a winter's night a traveler
like.r: A playful, much more theoretical novel made of interrupted stories.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: A romance that plays with time and memory, quirkier and sharper.

h: A murdered teenager watches from heaven as her family breaks and her killer carries on in a quiet Pennsylvania suburb.

like.r: Another popular mystery narrated by an unusual voice, funnier and more comic about a family.

t: The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time
